values: coupling
no-import-outside-roots
Production code imports a project module outside `python.sourceRoots`.
Code outside the source roots is not checked by the gate, so production code must not depend on it.
Move the imported code under a source root, or add its folder to `python.sourceRoots` so the gate checks it.
no-production-cycles
A module that is in an import cycle with other modules of its package.
A cycle makes modules impossible to load, test or replace one at a time.
Move what they share into a module both import, or pass it in instead of importing it back.
package-cycle
A package that is in a dependency cycle with other packages.
A cycle makes packages impossible to load, test or replace one at a time.
Move the shared types down into one of them, or invert one dependency behind an interface.
python-rules
any-in-domain
`<name>` uses `Any` in domain code
One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
Use the real type, a `Protocol`, a `TypeVar` or a frozen dataclass; parse untrusted data at the boundary so the domain only sees typed values.
blind-suppress
`<name>` ignores every error
Name the expected exception: `contextlib.suppress(KeyError)`; or handle it or re-raise it with its cause. In a test, use `pytest.raises(SpecificError)` (`self.assertRaises` in unittest).
boolean-flag-parameter
`<name>` switches a public function between two behaviors

Make the flag keyword-only, `def send(message, *, urgent=False)`, split the function into two named for each behavior, or pass an enum. click, typer and FastAPI pass options by keyword, so `def command(*, verbose: bool)` works there. A method that overrides a base class takes `@typing.override` (`typing_extensions.override` before Python 3.12), which lifts the rule.
cancellation-not-propagated
`<name>` has a path that consumes cancellation or replaces it with another error

After cleanup, use a bare `raise` or re-raise the unchanged caught cancellation. Keep intentional cancellation boundaries in the backend's timeout or cancellation scope; returning a failure result or chaining another error does not propagate cancellation.
catch-log-without-exception
`<name>` logs a caught error without its traceback
Keep the traceback: `logger.exception("message")` or `logger.error("message", exc_info=True)`; the exception as an argument drops it. Re-raising after the log also passes.
clock-now
`<name>()` reads the clock in domain code
Take the time as a parameter or a `Callable[[], datetime]` and call `datetime.now(tz=UTC)` in the composition root.
compatibility-shim
`<name>` keeps an old name working

When code moves or is renamed, change every caller in the same change and delete the old name: keep no alias, forwarding function, module `__getattr__`, `@deprecated` marker or deprecation warning. A published library keeps the deprecation of its public names, and that path takes an exception.
credential-shape
A string has the shape of a credential
Read the credential from the environment in the composition root and pass it in; never commit a key, token, private key or URL with a password.
enum-string-constants
<name> are string constants that belong in one enum
Declare an enum: `class Status(enum.StrEnum): ACTIVE = "active"` on Python 3.11+, otherwise `class Status(str, enum.Enum)`.
falsy-default
`<name>` replaces a falsy argument with a default, so `0`, `""`, `[]` and `False` count as not given
Test for `None` only: `limit if limit is not None else DEFAULT_LIMIT`, or `if limit is None: limit = DEFAULT_LIMIT`.
frozen-dataclass
Dataclass <name> is not frozen
Declare records as `@dataclass(frozen=True)` and build a changed copy with `dataclasses.replace`.
generic-name
`<name>` has a generic name
Name it for its job (`price_rounding.py`, `OrderRepository`); shared logic that belongs to no feature lives in `shared/` under a name that says what it does.
handwritten-boundary-guard
`<name>` checks untrusted data by hand
Parse untrusted input once at the boundary with pydantic (`Model.model_validate(data)`) in an `adapters/` package, not with `isinstance` checks or a `TypeGuard`.
hardcoded-secret
`<name>` holds a hardcoded secret
Read the secret from the environment in the composition root (`os.environ["API_TOKEN"]`) and pass it in; keep placeholders such as `"changeme"` out of production code.
http-without-timeout
`<name>` can wait forever: it has no timeout

Pass a timeout in seconds: `urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10)`, `session.get(url, timeout=10)`, or set `socket.setdefaulttimeout(10)` once at startup for `urllib`; an `httpx` client keeps its 5 second default unless you pass another number (`httpx.Client(timeout=10)`), never `timeout=None`.
import-time-effect
`<name>()` runs when the module is imported, so every import, tests included, performs it
Move the call into a function and call that from the composition root (`main.py`, a `create_app` factory) or under `if __name__ == "__main__":`, passing the result in.
io-in-domain
`<name>` does input or output in domain code
Keep `domain/` pure: define a `Protocol` in the domain and implement it in `adapters/`, then pass the adapter in.
io-in-loop
`<name>` runs once per item of a loop

Batch it: fetch or write all items in one call, or run the calls together with a bounded `asyncio.gather` (a shared `asyncio.Semaphore` acquired in the task) or a `ThreadPoolExecutor.map` when there is no batch API.
logger-in-domain
`<name>` is imported into domain code
Return a result that says what happened, or raise a domain error, and let `adapters/` or the composition root log it.
module-level-mutable-state
`<name>` changes a module-level collection

Keep the state in an object that is created in the composition root and passed in, or build a new immutable value and return it. A registry filled once at import time (a decorator that adds the function to a table) is not run-time state; the exception route below covers its path.
module-state-in-domain
Domain code uses the module state `<name>`
Receive the state as a parameter and return the new value; the composition root creates the object and passes it in.
network-in-test
`<name>` reaches the network in a unit test
Replace the network with a fake: patch the client with `monkeypatch`, use `responses` or `respx`, or move the test to an `integration/` folder.
no-inline-suppression
Inline suppression `# <name>`
Remove the comment and fix the code.
no-type-check
`<name>` is excluded from type checking by `@no_type_check`
Remove the decorator and annotate the code so the checker can verify it.
not-type-checking
`<name>` hides code from the type checkers
Put the code in the normal flow; `if TYPE_CHECKING:` is only for imports that annotations need.
parameter-mutation
`<name>` changes the argument the caller passed in

Build and return a new value (`[*items, item]`, `{**table, key: value}`), or copy the argument first (`items = [*items]`) when the function needs a working copy; do not hand a result back through a parameter.
process-env-access
`<name>` reads the process environment outside the composition root
Read the environment once in the composition root (`main.py`, `settings.py`, a `composition_root/` package) and pass the values in as arguments or a frozen settings dataclass.
pydantic-any-field
The pydantic field `<name>` is typed `Any`
Give the field its real type (`str`, `int`, a nested model, `Literal[...]`) or constrain it with `Field(min_length=1)` so the model validates it.
pydantic-boundary
<name> is imported outside an adapters/ package
Use pydantic only in an `adapters/` package to parse untrusted input (`Model.model_validate(data)`), and pass frozen dataclasses on from there.
pydantic-extra-allow
The pydantic model `<name>` accepts unknown fields
Set `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` (or leave the default `ignore`) and declare every field the model needs.
random-in-domain
`<name>()` draws randomness in domain code
Take the value, a `random.Random` or an id factory as a parameter and create it in the composition root.
random-in-test
`<name>()` draws random values in a test
Use fixed values, or seed the generator (`random.Random(42)`) and pass it in, so a failure reproduces.
real-clock-in-test
`<name>()` reads the real clock in a test
Freeze or inject the time: pass a fixed `datetime` in, use `freezegun` or `time_machine`, or patch the clock with `monkeypatch`.
repeated-string-literal
The string "<name>" is repeated three times or more
Name it once as a constant (`PENDING = "pending"`), or as a member of an enum when the strings form a set of states.
secret-in-log
`<name>` is a secret and is passed to a log call
Log that it is set (`logger.info("token set: %s", token is not None)`) or a masked tail, never the value.
service-locator-lookup
`<name>` looks a service up in a dependency-injection container, which hides what this code needs and fails only when it runs, if the registration is missing

Take the dependency as an argument typed with the narrow protocol the code needs, and resolve it once in the composition root (`main.py`, a `composition_root/` package, a `create_app` factory, or a file listed in "layout.entryPoints"). `@inject` with `Provide[...]` is the allowed wiring, and a lookup in an `injector.Module` or `Provider` or inside a registration factory (`di[Mailer] = lambda di: Mailer(di[Config])`, `container.register(Mailer, factory=make_mailer)`) is composition code.
shell-command
`<name>` runs a command through a shell
Run the program directly with the arguments as a list and leave the shell out: `subprocess.run(["git", "status"], check=True)`; `shell=False` is the default.
skipped-test-without-reason
`<name>` skips a test without a reason
Give the reason: `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="needs the staging database")`, `pytest.skip("...")`; or fix or delete the test.
sleep-in-test
`<name>` waits for real time in a test
Control the clock instead of waiting: inject a fake clock, patch `time.sleep` with `monkeypatch`, or poll a condition with a bounded retry helper.
sql-string-formatting
`<name>` runs a query built by formatting a string

Pass the values as query parameters: `cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (user_id,))`, `session.execute(text("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id"), {"id": user_id})` in SQLAlchemy, `Model.objects.raw("... WHERE id = %s", [user_id])` in Django. Build placeholder lists from placeholders alone (`", ".join(["%s"] * len(ids))`) and optional filters as `conditions.append("name = %s")` joined with `" AND "`. A table or column name comes from a fixed lookup (`COLUMNS[key]` over a dict of constant names), a check against a constant set that stops otherwise (`if column not in ALLOWED: raise ValueError(column)`), a `Literal[...]` or `Enum` value, the schema (`table.name`, `model._meta.db_table`), or a quoting call (`psycopg.sql.Identifier(name)`, `dialect.identifier_preparer.quote(name)`).
stub-beside-source
`<name>` sits beside its source and replaces it for the checkers
Delete the `.pyi` file and annotate the `.py` file itself.
swallowed-exception
`<name>` swallows the error: it only logs it or returns a default, and carries on

Re-raise it with its cause (`raise DomainError(...) from error`), return a failure result that carries the error (`return Rejected(str(error))`), or return the errors the function builds along with its result (`return results, errors`); logging alone is not handling. `contextlib.suppress(SpecificError)` ignores one expected error. In a test, use `pytest.raises(SpecificError)` (`self.assertRaises` in unittest).
task-outlives-resource
`<name>`: the resource closes when its `with` block ends, while the child task can still use it
Open the resource around the whole task group, or inside the child task.
tautological-assert
`<name>` can never fail
Assert on the result of the code under test: `assert total(order) == Decimal("12.50")`.
test-helper-in-source
`<name>` is test support inside the production source

Move test helpers and fixtures into the tests folder (`tests/support/`, `conftest.py`) so they do not ship with the package. A library's public `testing` module is allowed when the package `__init__.py` imports it or lists it in `__all__`.
test-without-assertion
Test `<name>` has no assertion
Assert the outcome: `assert result == expected`, `with pytest.raises(SomeError):`, or call one of the assertion helpers the project tests use.
tls-verification-off
`<name>` turns off TLS certificate verification, or lets the environment turn it off

Keep verification on in every environment and trust the certificate authority instead: `requests.get(url, verify="/etc/ssl/private-ca.pem", timeout=10)`, `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=ca_path)`, `tlsCAFile=ca_path` for MongoDB, or `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` and `SSL_CERT_FILE` pointing at the bundle. A server that asks for optional client certificates uses `ssl.create_default_context(ssl.Purpose.CLIENT_AUTH)` with `verify_mode = ssl.CERT_OPTIONAL`; a server context that loads its own certificate needs no `verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE` line: delete it.
todo-without-issue
The task marker `<name>` has no issue
Name the issue right after the marker (`# TODO(#123): ...`, `# TODO PROJ-123: ...` or a link), or delete the comment and track the work in the issue tracker.
tri-state-boolean
`<name>` is a boolean that can also be `None`, a third state

Name the three states with an enum (`class Consent(Enum)` with `GRANTED`, `DENIED` and `UNKNOWN`), or take a keyword-only `bool` with a default (`*, urgent: bool = False`) when `None` only means false. A method that overrides a base class takes `@typing.override` and keeps the base signature.
unbounded-fan-out
`<name>` starts `<call>` for every element of `<collection>` at once

A large collection exhausts the remote service's connections or rate limit. Hold one `asyncio.Semaphore(8)` created outside the tasks with `async with limit:` around each call, gather fixed-size slices (`items[i : i + 20]`), or make one batch call when the API has one.
uncollected-tests
`<name>` defines tests that the test run does not collect
Name the file so pytest collects it (`test_*.py` or `*_test.py`), or add its pattern to `python_files` in the pytest configuration.
unsafe-deserialization
`<name>` can build arbitrary Python objects from the document
Load YAML with `yaml.safe_load(text)`, `yaml.safe_load_all(text)` for several documents, or `Loader=yaml.SafeLoader` (or a subclass of it).
unsafe-path-join
`<name>()` builds a file path from its input without a containment check
Resolve the path and check it stays inside the base before using it: `target = (base / name).resolve()`, then `if not target.is_relative_to(base.resolve()): raise ValueError(...)`.
unshielded-cleanup-await
`<name>` can be cancelled before the cleanup finishes, so the resource may stay open

Run the cleanup in a shielded scope with a deadline: `with trio.CancelScope(deadline=trio.current_time() + 5, shield=True): await resource.aclose()` (`anyio.CancelScope(deadline=anyio.current_time() + 5, shield=True)` in AnyIO; `move_on_after(5, shield=True)` needs Trio 0.27 or later). A shield without a deadline can hang shutdown.
weak-hmac
`<name>` signs with HMAC-MD5, which is no longer approved for message authentication
Sign with `hmac.new(key, message, hashlib.sha256)` and compare with `hmac.compare_digest`; HMAC-SHA1 is accepted where a protocol fixes it (TOTP, OAuth 1.0a).
